A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same perspective article. Content can be matched across renamed and reorganized subsections. Both end with references; neither contains appendices.

before.justification: v1 presents literature-based discussion and research recommendations. Empirical examples are attributed to cited works; no original experimental or data-analysis results are reported.

after.justification: v2 remains a perspective article. Its expanded empirical examples summarize cited studies rather than experiments, simulations, user studies, or data analyses performed for this work.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an implemented algorithm or model. Added descriptions of efficient attention, causal models, and constrained generation concern existing research and future directions.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. Expanded discussion of multilingual systems and other applications does not constitute additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a comparator set against a proposed method. Additional cited methods are literature coverage, not experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 substantially expands discussion of evaluation metrics, but neither version specifies or applies an experimental evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Neither version presents its own ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary empirical analyses. Added failure examples summarize literature or explain research challenges.

E5.justification: The expanded uncertainty and calibration discussion concerns model behavior. Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical testing for this work.

E6.justification: v1 leaves watermark resistance to downstream transformations unclear; v2 Section 4.1 reports cited findings of evasion through small edits. Section 4.3 also adds literature-derived findings about language-dependent tokenization costs. These are qualitative additions, not original experiments. The cited 175B-parameter/80GB quantization example and 25–50 diffusion NFEs remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. Added explanations of uncertainty sources, calibration, and modeling assumptions remain conceptual background rather than new mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central thesis that scaling alone cannot resolve generative AI's shortcomings, and the same three contribution areas: adaptability, efficiency, and responsible deployment.

C2.justification: v2 substantially deepens the qualifications and mechanisms behind the recommendations. Section 2.2 adds risks from incorrect prior knowledge and difficult constraints; Section 3.2 discusses evaluator feedback biases and competing calibration targets; Sections 4.3–4.5 expand fairness tradeoffs, limitations of mechanistic explanations, and obstacles to enforcing hard constraints.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies original implementation or experimental details. Section 3.2 changes the Parti-prompts shortlink to a named Open Parti Prompts Leaderboard address, but the PDFs alone do not establish whether this changes the resource provided or merely its link.

R1.justification: The literature treatment expands substantially, including FlashAttention and GQA, model-based evaluation, multilingual tokenization fairness, mechanistic interpretability, and constrained decoding. Some earlier heavy-tailed modeling references disappear. These are substantive changes beyond citation-style and publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: Extensive paragraph rewrites and explanatory expansions affect Sections 1–4. Uncertainty material from v1 Section 4.5 and calibration discussion from Section 3.2 are regrouped and expanded, particularly in v2 Section 4.1. Several subsections are renamed, Clara Meister is added as an author, and the funding-disclosure section is removed.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively retypeset, with a wider text block, different typography and heading styles, running top rules, redesigned title and front matter, and an unnumbered author-year bibliography. Neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: For a perspective article, v2 substantially improves the research roadmap by supplying concrete failure mechanisms and qualifications where v1 offers briefer recommendations. The discussions of incorrect priors, evaluation feedback biases, calibration targets, and interpretability validation make the argument more precise and balanced. Removing the funding disclosure reduces transparency, but the gains in critical depth across central sections outweigh that loss.
